the structure and function of the micronemal protein complex of Toxoplas gondii, a protozoan parasite that causes toxoplasmosis in humans and animals.
the structure-function relationship of TgMICs, and the role they play in the invasion of T. gondiitachyzoites into host cells.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the TgMICs are a complex of micronemal adhesion complexes, each of which is composed of a number of different subunits, and that the TgMic1 Galectin domain is critical for the folding, assembly, and transport of the MIC4-MIC1 complex.
the Galectin-like structure from TgMIC 1 is involved in the folding, assembly and trafficking of the MIC1-MIC4-MIC6 complex.
the Galectin-like domains of TgMIC4 and TgMIC1 have evolved to function in different ways.

TgMIC1 plays multiple roles in the assembly, transport, and adhesion of the complex.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Galectin-like domains are not necessarily involved in carbohydrate recognition, but can be used as an additional scaffold for the formation of protein complexes.

the TgMICs represent an excellent system for studying protein-protein interactions in apicomplexan parasite biology and that the Galectin-like protein domain is an important new player in this system.
